newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rulers popularity keeps dropping.
newsitem.headline: French rulers popularity keeps dropping.

text.p: The popularity of French Prime Minister Alain Juppe dropped sharply after he unveiled an austerity budget last month, according to an opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The Louis Harris poll of 1,003 voters said the percentage of people unhappy with Juppe jumped to 64 from 55 percent while his supporters dropped to 30 from 34 percent.

The poll was carried out on September 23-24, less than a week after Juppe announced a draft 1997 budget cutting public spending to curb state deficit to allow France to join the European single currency in 1999.
The percentage of voters satisfied with President Jacques Chirac rose to 39 percent from 38 percent, but those unhappy with him increased more sharply to 55 from 50 percent.

The survey said voters were markedly more pessimistic, with 65 percent believing the economic and social situation was deteriorating, compared with 62 percent a month ago. Only four percent believed it was improving.

Juppe made a much-publicised announcement last month that income tax would be reduced next year but the simultaneous announcement that the cuts would be compensated by hefty hikes in indirect taxes led to much derision directed against him.
The government's popularity is also strongly affected by increasing widespread unemployment which Chirac had promised to curb when he came to power last year.
